question: _______ grows well on well-drained fertile soils in the flood plains of India where soils are renewed every year.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Jute is a natural fiber with high tensile strength and low extensibility, which makes it ideal for making strong and durable products like sacks and bags.

• It thrives in well-drained fertile soils found in the flood plains of India, where the soil is renewed annually by the silt deposition from the floods.

• Jute is primarily grown in the eastern parts of India, particularly in the states of West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, and Odisha.

• The jute plant requires a warm and humid climate, with temperatures ranging from 24°C to 37°C and relative humidity of 70% to 90%, conditions that are prevalent in these regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Natural Silk**

• Natural silk is a protein fiber produced by silkworms, primarily the larvae of the mulberry silkworm Bombyx mori.

• It is highly valued for its soft texture, sheen, and durability, making it ideal for fine textiles and clothing.

• The production of natural silk is known as sericulture, which involves the cultivation of silkworms and the extraction of silk from their cocoons.

• Silk production requires specific environmental conditions, including a warm climate and access to mulberry leaves, the primary food source for silkworms.

• **Saffron**

• Saffron is a spice derived from the flower of Crocus sativus, commonly known as the "saffron crocus."

• It is known for its distinct flavor, aroma, and vibrant color, making it a highly sought-after ingredient in culinary and medicinal applications.

• Saffron cultivation is labor-intensive and requires specific climatic conditions, including well-drained soil, moderate rainfall, and a warm climate.

• India, particularly the region of Kashmir, is one of the major producers of high-quality saffron in the world.

• **Bajra**

• Bajra, also known as pearl millet, is a drought-resistant cereal crop that thrives in arid and semi-arid regions.

• It is a staple food in many parts of India and is known for its high nutritional value, including proteins, fiber, and essential minerals.

• Bajra requires well-drained sandy loam soils and can be grown in areas with low rainfall and high temperatures.

• The crop is typically sown during the monsoon season and harvested within 3 to 4 months.
